CHA2DS2-VASc 9: acute-on-chronic combined systolic/diastolic heart failure and hypertensive heart disease with heart failure (Conditions 54c6281d, f89796e6) = 1; essential hypertension (Condition 44676e92) = 1; age 80 (>=75) = 2; type 2 diabetes (Condition 2547c8a4) = 1; prior cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia (Condition 8f7e95ca) = 2; atherosclerotic coronary disease (Condition db41b03a) = 1; female sex = 1. She is on aspirin and gabapentin only - no anticoagulant order is active and none is listed in any clinic note. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is missing.

71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation on the problem list (Condition 7010d0e5, 2025-08-22) and in the history line of every cardiology clinic note including the most recent (1a51402c, 2026-06-27). CHA2DS2-VASc 3: essential hypertension (Condition a85598ce) = 1; age 65-74 = 1; coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery (Condition 75b86cdb) = 1. Current medications are levothyroxine only (note 1a51402c); there is no active anticoagulant order. A score of 3 in a man is a class I indication for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of anticoagulation needs review (the remote peri-procedural haemorrhage, Condition 63df7d4c, should be weighed but is not by itself an absolute contraindication).

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic visit (MedicationRequest a0184d35, valid 2026-08-20 to 2027-01-04) and is the current anticoagulant. Eight days earlier the clinic filed a summary of outside records (DocumentReference 8fcbd349, 2026-08-12) documenting a 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 admission at Mercy Hospital for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9, two units transfused, with apixaban explicitly HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. The 2026-08-20 note simply continues apixaban (No changes today) without addressing the bleed or the hold, so the anticoagulant is being continued despite a documented reason it should not continue without review.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current. At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban (note a80a007c), and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was ordered (MedicationRequest 7c496afb, valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-23), but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (MedicationRequest c4b6df94, valid 2026-07-15 to 2027-01-03) and was not stopped. The same note lists both Apixaban 5 mg twice daily and Rivaroxaban 20 mg daily under current medications. Both orders are still in force at the evaluation time, so the patient is on duplicate anticoagulation (additionally with clopidogrel).

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 (DocumentReference 96cdf346) states: ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: ECG 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13:50) and ECG 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36:45) each show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation at about 130-140 bpm (RR intervals ranging 0.35-0.72 s). The documented rhythm and rate are both inconsistent with the same-day tracings.

Patient is on amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, with a current clinic order (MedicationRequest e78404bf, 2026-07-12 to 2027-01-09). His most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 536 ms and RR 0.97 s, giving a Bazett QTc of about 545 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo (clinic document 615f2777). QTc was 444 ms on the preceding tracing (108780865, 2025-06-07), i.e. a marked interval increase after amiodarone was started on 2025-11-10. Most recent electrolytes are normal (potassium 4.3 mmol/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, both 2026-06-09), so prescriber review of the amiodarone is required.

Patient takes escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, on a current clinic order (MedicationRequest 438668cc, 2026-07-18 to 2026-12-26; continuously refilled since it was started on 2024-05-14). Her most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) is sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 494 ms and RR 0.88 s, giving a Bazett QTc of about 527 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold of the QT monitoring memo (clinic document 615f2777). Note that the 2024-05-14 note described this same tracing as QT acceptable, which is not supported by the measurement (the preceding ECG 100065910 of 2022-11-23 had a QTc of 370 ms). Most recent potassium 3.8 mmol/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 2026-03-18) are low-normal. Prescriber review of escitalopram and a repeat ECG are needed.

Patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, on a current clinic order (MedicationRequest 62da0901, 2026-07-15 to 2027-01-07; citalopram has been refilled continuously since 2023-10-02). interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 0.66-0.86 s). Upright P wave in II (0.21 mV) before every QRS, PR 185 ms. Narrow QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal QRS axis +47 degrees (normal). QT 340 ms at RR 0.74 s gives a Bazett QTc of 395 ms. This is the patient's only ECG, so there is no prior tracing for comparison. Concordant with the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm, regular. Prominent upright P in II (0.22 mV), PR 142 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +39 degrees. QT 340 ms at RR 0.58 s, Bazett QTc 447 ms. The prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with a QTc of 592 ms; the QTc has fallen by about 145 ms, a decrease of more than 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 108 bpm. Upright P wave in II (0.12 mV) before each QRS, PR about 120 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees. QT 336 ms at RR 0.55 s, Bazett QTc 451 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response at about 136 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.35-0.65 s) and there is no discrete P wave in any lead on the averaged beat, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +8 degrees. There is widespread rate-related ST depression. QT about 292 ms, Bazett QTc 440 ms. The prior tracing 107914094, recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same day, is also atrial fibrillation at 132 bpm with QTc 443 ms, so there is no change. Note that the clinic note of 2026-06-10 describes this study as normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which the tracings contradict.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 0.87 s, RR variability under 1 per cent) with a low-amplitude atrial deflection preceding each QRS at a fixed interval of about 160 ms. The P wave is positive in I and aVL but negative in II, III and aVF (P axis roughly -45 degrees), which is not a sinus P axis: this is an ectopic low/left atrial rhythm rather than sinus rhythm. QRS 66 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -24 degrees. QT 410 ms, Bazett QTc 439 ms. The prior tracing 104232242 (2025-04-27) showed a rate of 61 bpm with markedly different limb-lead polarity (deep S in lead I, axis -175 degrees, suggesting arm-lead reversal on that study) and a QTc of 414 ms; no atrial fibrillation, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block on either study, and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm, regular (RR 0.62 s). Upright P wave in II (0.19 mV), PR about 116 ms. QRS 68 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +5 degrees. The T wave has a prominent late low-amplitude component; measuring to the end of the T wave gives QT about 370 ms and a Bazett QTc of about 470 ms (measuring by the tangent method to the steep limb alone would give roughly 380 ms). Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.
Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR 0.83 s). Upright P in II, PR 144 ms. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +21 degrees. QT 382 ms, Bazett QTc 419 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a controlled ventricular response, mean rate about 61 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.69-1.16 s, RMSSD 288 ms) and there are no P waves, so no PR interval can be given. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +27 degrees. Repolarisation is prolonged: on the long-cycle beats the T wave ends about 500-510 ms after QRS onset, giving QT roughly 530-545 ms at RR about 1.14 s and a Bazett QTc of about 505 ms. The prior ECG 107873952 (2024-11-12, three days earlier) was sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with PR 178 ms and QTc 418 ms, so this tracing shows new atrial fibrillation and a QTc increase of more than 60 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with sinus arrhythmia. Tall upright P in II (0.21 mV), PR about 112 ms. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +62 degrees. QT 424 ms at RR 1.03 s, Bazett QTc 418 ms. The prior ECG 106045460 (2025-03-08, one day earlier) is essentially identical (sinus 62 bpm, PR 112 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 438 ms); no change.

Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, regular (RR 0.72 s). Upright P in II (0.12 mV), PR 154 ms. Narrow QRS 60 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +53 degrees. QT 338 ms, Bazett QTc 398 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 76 bpm, regular (RR 0.78 s). Prominent upright P in II (0.27 mV), PR 154 ms. QRS 64 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +63 degrees. The T wave is broad with a long terminal limb ending about 440 ms after QRS onset: QT about 466 ms, Bazett QTc about 526 ms (prolonged). The prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02) had a QTc of 538 ms, so the QTc is essentially unchanged (-12 ms) and there is no change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, perfectly regular (RR 0.50 s). Upright P in II (0.21 mV) preceding each QRS with PR about 190 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +49 degrees. QT 282 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. Compared with the prior tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 175 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 424 ms, axis +49) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or repolarisation (QTc change -24 ms).

Sinus bradycardia at 55 bpm (RR 1.10 s). An upright P wave in II (0.10 mV) precedes each QRS but the PR interval is prolonged at about 215 ms, consistent with first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms with a dominant R wave in V1 (0.65 mV); no bundle branch block by duration. Axis +8 degrees. QT 408 ms, Bazett QTc 389 ms. The prior ECG 103042067 (2024-11-30) was sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm with PR about 190 ms, QRS 80 ms and QTc 369 ms - no new bundle branch block and no QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response at about 151 bpm. RR intervals vary from 0.29 to 0.58 s with no pattern and there is no organised atrial activity, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 66 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -5 degrees. QT 248 ms at mean RR 0.40 s, Bazett QTc 394 ms. The prior ECG 107374881 (2025-09-12, the previous day) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with an upright P in II and PR about 155 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm. Tall upright P in II (0.21 mV), PR 170 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +11 degrees. QT 374 ms at RR 0.83 s, Bazett QTc 409 ms. The prior ECG 105362569 (2025-11-21) was sinus rhythm at 67 bpm with a QTc of 539 ms; the QTc has fallen by about 130 ms, a decrease of more than 60 ms. Concordant with the 2025-11-23 note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular (RR 0.81 s). Upright P in II, PR about 190 ms (upper normal). QRS 82 ms with a deep S wave in lead I; no bundle branch block. Axis +57 degrees. QT 394 ms, Bazett QTc 437 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular. Upright P in II (0.15 mV), PR 130 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +45 degrees. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged: T wave peaks about 370 ms after QRS onset and ends near 465 ms, giving QT about 494 ms at RR 0.88 s and a Bazett QTc of about 526 ms. The previous ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23) had a QTc of 370 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. Clinically relevant because the patient takes escitalopram (QT watch-list drug).

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR 0.50 s). A discrete upright P wave in II precedes each QRS with PR about 140 ms; atrial activity is 1:1 with the ventricles and phase locked, excluding flutter. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +68 degrees. There is marked ST depression inferolaterally. QT about 294 ms, Bazett QTc 417 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm. Upright P in II (0.17 mV), PR 148 ms. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +57 degrees. QT 350 ms at RR 0.59 s, Bazett QTc 455 ms. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day (2021-08-23 10:06) and is essentially identical (sinus 100 bpm, PR 148 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 452 ms), so there is no interval change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular (RR 1.16 s). Upright P in II, PR 170 ms. QRS 84 ms with a tall R in V6 (3.3 mV) meeting voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy; no bundle branch block. Axis +35 degrees. QT 440 ms, Bazett QTc 408 ms. Prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) showed sinus bradycardia 58 bpm with an atrial ectopic beat, QRS 82 ms, QTc 422 ms - no significant change.

Sinus tachycardia at 122 bpm, regular. Upright P in II (0.15 mV), PR about 130 ms. QRS is now narrow at 86 ms; frontal axis +137 degrees (right axis deviation) with an rS pattern in lead I. QT 302 ms, Bazett QTc 430 ms. The prior tracing 106516875, recorded 13 hours earlier the same day (2024-12-05 01:33), showed a wide QRS of 144 ms with an rsR' in V1 and wide terminal S waves in I and V6 - right bundle branch block - together with an extreme axis of -177 degrees and QTc 475 ms. The bundle branch block has resolved on the current tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, regular (RR 0.97 s). Low-amplitude but consistent upright P in II, PR 170 ms. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +65 degrees. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad late T wave peaking about 405 ms after QRS onset and ending near 490 ms: QT about 536 ms, Bazett QTc 545 ms. The prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07) had a QTc of 450 ms, so the QTc has risen by about 95 ms, coinciding with amiodarone started 2025-11-10.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 100 bpm. The rhythm is grossly irregularly irregular (RR 0.39-1.07 s, RMSSD 243 ms) and there is no organised atrial activity - the TP segments are flat with no P waves on the averaged beat, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -49 degrees (left axis deviation). QT 330 ms, Bazett QTc 427 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 108 bpm. Upright P wave in II (0.12 mV) before each QRS, PR about 120 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees. QT 336 ms at RR 0.55 s, Bazett QTc 451 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response at about 136 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.35-0.65 s) and there is no discrete P wave in any lead on the averaged beat, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +8 degrees. There is widespread rate-related ST depression. QT about 292 ms, Bazett QTc 440 ms. The prior tracing 107914094, recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same day, is also atrial fibrillation at 132 bpm with QTc 443 ms, so there is no change. Note that the clinic note of 2026-06-10 describes this study as normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which the tracings contradict.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 0.87 s, RR variability under 1 per cent) with a low-amplitude atrial deflection preceding each QRS at a fixed interval of about 160 ms. The P wave is positive in I and aVL but negative in II, III and aVF (P axis roughly -45 degrees), which is not a sinus P axis: this is an ectopic low/left atrial rhythm rather than sinus rhythm. QRS 66 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -24 degrees. QT 410 ms, Bazett QTc 439 ms. The prior tracing 104232242 (2025-04-27) showed a rate of 61 bpm with markedly different limb-lead polarity (deep S in lead I, axis -175 degrees, suggesting arm-lead reversal on that study) and a QTc of 414 ms; no atrial fibrillation, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block on either study, and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm, regular (RR 0.62 s). Upright P wave in II (0.19 mV), PR about 116 ms. QRS 68 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +5 degrees. The T wave has a prominent late low-amplitude component; measuring to the end of the T wave gives QT about 370 ms and a Bazett QTc of about 470 ms (measuring by the tangent method to the steep limb alone would give roughly 380 ms). Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.
Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR 0.83 s). Upright P in II, PR 144 ms. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +21 degrees. QT 382 ms, Bazett QTc 419 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a controlled ventricular response, mean rate about 61 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.69-1.16 s, RMSSD 288 ms) and there are no P waves, so no PR interval can be given. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +27 degrees. Repolarisation is prolonged: on the long-cycle beats the T wave ends about 500-510 ms after QRS onset, giving QT roughly 530-545 ms at RR about 1.14 s and a Bazett QTc of about 505 ms. Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with sinus arrhythmia. Tall upright P in II (0.21 mV), PR about 112 ms. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +62 degrees. QT 424 ms at RR 1.03 s, Bazett QTc 418 ms. The prior ECG 106045460 (2025-03-08, one day earlier) is essentially identical (sinus 62 bpm, PR 112 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 438 ms); no change.

Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, regular (RR 0.72 s). Upright P in II (0.12 mV), PR 154 ms. Narrow QRS 60 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +53 degrees. QT 338 ms, Bazett QTc 398 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 76 bpm, regular (RR 0.78 s). Prominent upright P in II (0.27 mV), PR 154 ms. QRS 64 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +63 degrees. The T wave is broad with a long terminal limb ending about 440 ms after QRS onset: QT about 466 ms, Bazett QTc about 526 ms (prolonged). The prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02) had a QTc of 538 ms, so the QTc is essentially unchanged (-12 ms) and there is no change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, perfectly regular (RR 0.50 s). Upright P in II (0.21 mV) preceding each QRS with PR about 190 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +49 degrees. Compared with the prior tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 175 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 424 ms, axis +49) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or repolarisation (QTc change -24 ms).

Sinus bradycardia at 55 bpm (RR 1.10 s). An upright P wave in II (0.10 mV) precedes each QRS but the PR interval is prolonged at about 215 ms, consistent with first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms with a dominant R wave in V1 (0.65 mV); no bundle branch block by duration. Axis +8 degrees. QT 408 ms, Bazett QTc 389 ms. The prior ECG 103042067 (2024-11-30) was sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm with PR about 190 ms, QRS 80 ms and QTc 369 ms - no new bundle branch block and no QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response at about 151 bpm. RR intervals vary from 0.29 to 0.58 s with no pattern and there is no organised atrial activity, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 66 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -5 degrees. QT 248 ms at mean RR 0.40 s, Bazett QTc 394 ms. The prior ECG 107374881 (2025-09-12, the previous day) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with an upright P in II and PR about 155 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm. Tall upright P in II (0.21 mV), PR 170 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +11 degrees. QT 374 ms at RR 0.83 s, Bazett QTc 409 ms. The prior ECG 105362569 (2025-11-21) was sinus rhythm at 67 bpm with a QTc of 539 ms; the QTc has fallen by about 130 ms, a decrease of more than 60 ms. Concordant with the 2025-11-23 note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular (RR 0.81 s). Upright P in II, PR about 190 ms (upper normal). QRS 82 ms with a deep S wave in lead I; no bundle branch block. Axis +57 degrees. QT 394 ms, Bazett QTc 437 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, metronomically regular (RR 0.538 s, RR variability 0.2 per cent). A discrete atrial complex precedes each QRS - upright in II (0.20 mV) and biphasic in V1 - with PR about 166 ms; the T wave is inverted in II and upright in V1, which accounts for the unusual-looking baseline, and there is no sawtooth flutter activity. QRS 86 ms with a very deep S in V1 (2.9 mV); no bundle branch block. Axis +36 degrees. QT 310 ms, Bazett QTc 423 ms. The prior ECG 102955795 (2022-07-04) is very similar (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 415 ms), so there is no change.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular. Upright P in II (0.15 mV), PR 130 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +45 degrees. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged: T wave peaks about 370 ms after QRS onset and ends near 465 ms, giving QT about 494 ms at RR 0.88 s and a Bazett QTc of about 526 ms. The previous ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23) had a QTc of 370 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. Clinically relevant because the patient takes escitalopram (QT watch-list drug).

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR 0.50 s). A discrete upright P wave in II precedes each QRS with PR about 140 ms; atrial activity is 1:1 with the ventricles and phase locked, excluding flutter. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +68 degrees. There is marked ST depression inferolaterally. QT about 294 ms, Bazett QTc 417 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm. Upright P in II (0.17 mV), PR 148 ms. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +57 degrees. QT 350 ms at RR 0.59 s, Bazett QTc 455 ms. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day (2021-08-23 10:06) and is essentially identical (sinus 100 bpm, PR 148 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 452 ms), so there is no interval change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular (RR 1.16 s). Upright P in II, PR 170 ms. QRS 84 ms with a tall R in V6 (3.3 mV) meeting voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy; no bundle branch block. QT 302 ms, Bazett QTc 430 ms. The prior tracing 106516875, recorded 13 hours earlier the same day (2024-12-05 01:33), showed a wide QRS of 144 ms with an rsR' in V1 and wide terminal S waves in I and V6 - right bundle branch block - together with an extreme axis of -177 degrees and QTc 475 ms. The bundle branch block has resolved on the current tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, regular (RR 0.97 s). Low-amplitude but consistent upright P in II, PR 170 ms. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +65 degrees. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad late T wave peaking about 405 ms after QRS onset and ending near 490 ms: QT about 536 ms, Bazett QTc 545 ms. The prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07) had a QTc of 450 ms, so the QTc has risen by about 95 ms, coinciding with amiodarone started 2025-11-10.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 100 bpm. The rhythm is grossly irregularly irregular (RR 0.39-1.07 s, RMSSD 243 ms) and there is no organised atrial activity - the TP segments are flat with no P waves on the averaged beat, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -49 degrees (left axis deviation). QT 330 ms, Bazett QTc 427 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

CHA2DS2-VASc 5: hypertension (Condition ee66ac4a), age 65-74, prior cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia (Conditions 8f42f0e4 / 6fbf21c2), female sex. No anticoagulant is on the current medication list - the most recent cardiology clinic notes (through 2026-06-23) list only famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol, and there is no active anticoagulant order. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is not being given; needs review.

Patient takes amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, on a current clinic order (MedicationRequest c67148bf, 2026-06-17 to 2027-01-06). Her most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with a markedly prolonged QT of about 586 ms at RR 1.04 s, giving a Bazett QTc of roughly 574 ms - far above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo (clinic document 615f2777). The preceding tracing (100867733, 2022-04-06, atrial fibrillation at 130 bpm) had a QTc of 426 ms. Most recent potassium 4.2 mmol/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 2026-06-17) are normal. She is also 95 years old and on warfarin; prescriber review of the amiodarone and a current ECG are required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (MedicationRequest 5d345f42; amiodarone first appears in the medication list of clinic note aa0ab6aa of that date, the only prior exposure being an inpatient course in January 2025). The start date falls between 2025-09-01 and 2026-03-01, so the original memo applies (clinic document e25bb79f): an ECG within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met on time.

ECG 101538691 was recorded on 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met on time.

The start is on or after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo applies (clinic document 2a70ec05): ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07 (documented in note 56ca7667 as sinus rhythm), 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met on time.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (MedicationRequest ead8699a; no earlier escitalopram order). The start is after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo applies (clinic document 2a70ec05): ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-04-24. The only ECG for this patient (107859369) was recorded on 2026-04-29, five days after the deadline, so no ECG was obtained within the required window and the requirement was not met by its due date.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (MedicationRequest 9fa1dfe1; the only previous exposure was a brief inpatient order 2025-12-30 to 2026-01-01, so this is a new start at a clinic visit). The start is after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo applies (clinic document 2a70ec05): ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-15. The patient has only one ECG in the chart (106035722, 2025-12-25), long before the start, and no ECG has been done since. The requirement is past due and unmet.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (MedicationRequest d7292a2a; previous exposure was inpatient only, in 2024). The start is after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo applies (clinic document 2a70ec05): ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-24. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, but the nursing telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference 5e12a8aa) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - inside the 14-day window - and that the report was requested by fax but has not been received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (MedicationRequest 34d26a30; previous exposure was inpatient only, in February-March 2025). The start is after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo applies (clinic document 2a70ec05): ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been recorded since the start (the most recent tracings are 106045460 and 104253928 from March 2025), but the deadline is after the 2026-09-24 evaluation date, so the ECG is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr Kessler documented a warfarin dose change in the note itself (DocumentReference b32487e8): INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR. Under the 2026-03-01 memo (clinic document 372c7683) an INR is required within 7 days of a dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05 (Observation 4282f19b), four days after the change, so the requirement was met on time.

On 2026-09-10 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist documented a warfarin dose change in the note that made it (DocumentReference 9579a764): Home INR 3.4. Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol. Clinic pharmacists are authorised to adjust warfarin under the standing order (clinic document a82fdaa4), so the 2026-03-01 memo applies (clinic document 372c7683): INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The last INR in the chart is 2.7 on 2026-06-17 (Observation bb649b59); no INR has been obtained since the dose change, and the due date has passed.

80-year-old woman (DOB 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 2025-09-12 through 2026-06-22 (most recent note f0a45897, 2026-06-22). CHA2DS2-VASc 9: acute-on-chronic combined systolic/diastolic heart failure and hypertensive heart disease with heart failure (Conditions 54c6281d, f89796e6) = 1; essential hypertension (Condition 44676e92) = 1; age 80 (>=75) = 2; type 2 diabetes (Condition 2547c8a4) = 1; prior cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia (Condition 8f7e95ca) = 2; atherosclerotic coronary disease (Condition db41b03a) = 1; female sex = 1. She is on aspirin and gabapentin only - no anticoagulant order is active and none is listed in any clinic note. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is missing.

71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation on the problem list (Condition 7010d0e5, 2025-08-22) and in the history line of every cardiology clinic note including the most recent (1a51402c, 2026-06-27). CHA2DS2-VASc 3: essential hypertension (Condition a85598ce) = 1; age 65-74 = 1; coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery (Condition 75b86cdb) = 1. Current medications are levothyroxine only (note 1a51402c); there is no active anticoagulant order. A score of 3 in a man is a class I indication for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of anticoagulation needs review (the remote peri-procedural haemorrhage, Condition 63df7d4c, should be weighed but is not by itself an absolute contraindication).

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic visit (MedicationRequest a0184d35, valid 2026-08-20 to 2027-01-04) and is the current anticoagulant. Eight days earlier the clinic filed a summary of outside records (DocumentReference 8fcbd349, 2026-08-12) documenting a 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 admission at Mercy Hospital for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9, two units transfused, with apixaban explicitly HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. The 2026-08-20 note simply continues apixaban (No changes today) without addressing the bleed or the hold, so the anticoagulant is being continued despite a documented reason it should not continue without review.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current. At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban (note a80a007c), and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was ordered (MedicationRequest 7c496afb, valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-23), but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (MedicationRequest c4b6df94, valid 2026-07-15 to 2027-01-03) and was not stopped. The same note lists both Apixaban 5 mg twice daily and Rivaroxaban 20 mg daily under current medications. Both orders are still in force at the evaluation time, so the patient is on duplicate anticoagulation (additionally with clopidogrel).

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 (DocumentReference 96cdf346) states: ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: ECG 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13:50) and ECG 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36:45) each show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation at about 130-140 bpm (RR intervals ranging 0.35-0.72 s). The documented rhythm and rate are both inconsistent with the same-day tracings.

Patient is on amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, with a current clinic order (MedicationRequest e78404bf, 2026-07-12 to 2027-01-09). His most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 536 ms and RR 0.97 s, giving a Bazett QTc of about 545 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo (clinic document 615f2777). QTc was 444 ms on the preceding tracing (108780865, 2025-06-07), i.e. a marked interval increase after amiodarone was started on 2025-11-10. Most recent electrolytes are normal (potassium 4.3 mmol/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, both 2026-06-09), so prescriber review of the amiodarone is required.

Patient takes escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, on a current clinic order (MedicationRequest 438668cc, 2026-07-18 to 2026-12-26; continuously refilled since it was started on 2024-05-14). Her most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) is sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 494 ms and RR 0.88 s, giving a Bazett QTc of about 527 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold of the QT monitoring memo (clinic document 615f2777). Note that the 2024-05-14 note described this same tracing as QT acceptable, which is not supported by the measurement (the preceding ECG 100065910 of 2022-11-23 had a QTc of 370 ms). Most recent potassium 3.8 mmol/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 2026-03-18) are low-normal. Prescriber review of escitalopram and a repeat ECG are needed.

Patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, on a current clinic order (MedicationRequest 62da0901, 2026-07-15 to 2027-01-07; citalopram has been refilled continuously since 2023-10-02). The most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT 492 ms and RR 0.86 s, giving a Bazett QTc of about 531 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo (clinic document 615f2777); the previous tracing (107149156, 2020-06-17) had a QTc of 405 ms. Most recent potassium 4.6 mmol/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08) are normal. Citalopram 40 mg also exceeds the recommended maximum dose for QT risk, so prescriber review is required.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 0.66-0.86 s). Upright P wave in II (0.21 mV) before every QRS, PR 185 ms. Narrow QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal QRS axis +47 degrees (normal). QT 340 ms at RR 0.74 s gives a Bazett QTc of 395 ms. This is the patient's only ECG, so there is no prior tracing for comparison. Concordant with the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm, regular. Prominent upright P in II (0.22 mV), PR 142 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +39 degrees. QT 340 ms at RR 0.58 s, Bazett QTc 447 ms. The prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with a QTc of 592 ms; the QTc has fallen by about 145 ms, a decrease of more than 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 108 bpm. Upright P wave in II (0.12 mV) before each QRS, PR about 120 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees. QT 336 ms at RR 0.55 s, Bazett QTc 451 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response at about 136 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.35-0.65 s) and there is no discrete P wave in any lead on the averaged beat, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +8 degrees. There is widespread rate-related ST depression. QT about 292 ms, Bazett QTc 440 ms. The prior tracing 107914094, recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same day, is also atrial fibrillation at 132 bpm with QTc 443 ms, so there is no change. Note that the clinic note of 2026-06-10 describes this study as normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which the tracings contradict.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 0.87 s, RR variability under 1 per cent) with a low-amplitude atrial deflection preceding each QRS at a fixed interval of about 160 ms. The P wave is positive in I and aVL but negative in II, III and aVF (P axis roughly -45 degrees), which is not a sinus P axis: this is an ectopic low/left atrial rhythm rather than sinus rhythm. QRS 66 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -24 degrees. QT 410 ms, Bazett QTc 439 ms. The prior tracing 104232242 (2025-04-27) showed a rate of 61 bpm with markedly different limb-lead polarity (deep S in lead I, axis -175 degrees, suggesting arm-lead reversal on that study) and a QTc of 414 ms; no atrial fibrillation, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block on either study, and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm, regular (RR 0.62 s). Upright P wave in II (0.19 mV), PR about 116 ms. QRS 68 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +5 degrees. The T wave has a prominent late low-amplitude component; measuring to the end of the T wave gives QT about 370 ms and a Bazett QTc of about 470 ms (measuring by the tangent method to the steep limb alone would give roughly 380 ms). Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.
Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR 0.83 s). Upright P in II, PR 144 ms. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +21 degrees. QT 382 ms, Bazett QTc 419 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a controlled ventricular response, mean rate about 61 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.69-1.16 s, RMSSD 288 ms) and there are no P waves, so no PR interval can be given. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +27 degrees. Repolarisation is prolonged: on the long-cycle beats the T wave ends about 500-510 ms after QRS onset, giving QT roughly 530-545 ms at RR about 1.14 s and a Bazett QTc of about 505 ms. The prior ECG 107873952 (2024-11-12, three days earlier) was sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with PR 178 ms and QTc 418 ms, so this tracing shows new atrial fibrillation and a QTc increase of more than 60 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with sinus arrhythmia. Tall upright P in II (0.21 mV), PR about 112 ms. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +62 degrees. QT 424 ms at RR 1.03 s, Bazett QTc 418 ms. The prior ECG 106045460 (2025-03-08, one day earlier) is essentially identical (sinus 62 bpm, PR 112 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 438 ms); no change.

Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, regular (RR 0.72 s). Upright P in II (0.12 mV), PR 154 ms. Narrow QRS 60 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +53 degrees. QT 338 ms, Bazett QTc 398 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 76 bpm, regular (RR 0.78 s). Prominent upright P in II (0.27 mV), PR 154 ms. QRS 64 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +63 degrees. The T wave is broad with a long terminal limb ending about 440 ms after QRS onset: QT about 466 ms, Bazett QTc about 526 ms (prolonged). The prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02) had a QTc of 538 ms, so the QTc is essentially unchanged (-12 ms) and there is no change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, perfectly regular (RR 0.50 s). Upright P in II (0.21 mV) preceding each QRS with PR about 190 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +49 degrees. QT 282 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. Compared with the prior tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 175 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 424 ms, axis +49) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or repolarisation (QTc change -24 ms).

Sinus bradycardia at 55 bpm (RR 1.10 s). An upright P wave in II (0.10 mV) precedes each QRS but the PR interval is prolonged at about 215 ms, consistent with first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms with a dominant R wave in V1 (0.65 mV); no bundle branch block by duration. Axis +8 degrees. QT 408 ms, Bazett QTc 389 ms. The prior ECG 103042067 (2024-11-30) was sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm with PR about 190 ms, QRS 80 ms and QTc 369 ms - no new bundle branch block and no QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response at about 151 bpm. RR intervals vary from 0.29 to 0.58 s with no pattern and there is no organised atrial activity, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 66 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -5 degrees. QT 248 ms at mean RR 0.40 s, Bazett QTc 394 ms. The prior ECG 107374881 (2025-09-12, the previous day) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with an upright P in II and PR about 155 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm. Tall upright P in II (0.21 mV), PR 170 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +11 degrees. QT 374 ms at RR 0.83 s, Bazett QTc 409 ms. The prior ECG 105362569 (2025-11-21) was sinus rhythm at 67 bpm with a QTc of 539 ms; the QTc has fallen by about 130 ms, a decrease of more than 60 ms. Concordant with the 2025-11-23 note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular (RR 0.81 s). Upright P in II, PR about 190 ms (upper normal). QRS 82 ms with a deep S wave in lead I; no bundle branch block. Axis +57 degrees. QT 394 ms, Bazett QTc 437 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, metronomically regular (RR 0.538 s, RR variability 0.2 per cent). A discrete atrial complex precedes each QRS - upright in II (0.20 mV) and biphasic in V1 - with PR about 166 ms; the T wave is inverted in II and upright in V1, which accounts for the unusual-looking baseline, and there is no sawtooth flutter activity. QRS 86 ms with a very deep S in V1 (2.9 mV); no bundle branch block. Axis +36 degrees. QT 310 ms, Bazett QTc 423 ms. The prior ECG 102955795 (2022-07-04) is very similar (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 415 ms), so there is no change.

Sinus rhythm at a mean rate of 62 bpm. The baseline cycle length is constant at about 0.97 s with one early beat (RR 0.54 s) followed by a compensatory pause (RR 1.39 s) - a single atrial/ventricular ectopic beat. A broad upright P wave is present in II and I before each conducted beat with a PR interval of about 200 ms (upper limit of normal). QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -30 degrees (just within normal). QT 410 ms, Bazett QTc 416 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison. There is no atrial fibrillation on this tracing despite the paroxysmal AF diagnosis.

Regular rhythm at 70 bpm with a consistent atrial complex before each QRS at PR about 144 ms. The limb leads show a globally inverted pattern - lead I is almost entirely negative (S 1.4 mV), aVR is positive, and the P wave is negative in I and II - while the praecordial leads are unremarkable; this pattern is typical of right/left arm lead reversal (dextrocardia is the alternative). Taken at face value the frontal QRS axis is -173 degrees, i.e. in the extreme (northwest) quadrant. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block. QT 358 ms at RR 0.86 s, Bazett QTc 385 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular. Upright P in II (0.15 mV), PR 130 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +45 degrees. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged: T wave peaks about 370 ms after QRS onset and ends near 465 ms, giving QT about 494 ms at RR 0.88 s and a Bazett QTc of about 526 ms. The previous ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23) had a QTc of 370 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. Clinically relevant because the patient takes escitalopram (QT watch-list drug).

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR 0.50 s). A discrete upright P wave in II precedes each QRS with PR about 140 ms; atrial activity is 1:1 with the ventricles and phase locked, excluding flutter. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +68 degrees. There is marked ST depression inferolaterally. QT about 294 ms, Bazett QTc 417 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm. Upright P in II (0.17 mV), PR 148 ms. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +57 degrees. QT 350 ms at RR 0.59 s, Bazett QTc 455 ms. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day (2021-08-23 10:06) and is essentially identical (sinus 100 bpm, PR 148 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 452 ms), so there is no interval change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular (RR 1.16 s). Upright P in II, PR 170 ms. QRS 84 ms with a tall R in V6 (3.3 mV) meeting voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy; no bundle branch block. Axis +35 degrees. QT 440 ms, Bazett QTc 408 ms. Prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) showed sinus bradycardia 58 bpm with an atrial ectopic beat, QRS 82 ms, QTc 422 ms - no significant change.

Sinus tachycardia at 122 bpm, regular. Upright P in II (0.15 mV), PR about 130 ms. QRS is now narrow at 86 ms; frontal axis +137 degrees (right axis deviation) with an rS pattern in lead I. QT 302 ms, Bazett QTc 430 ms. The prior tracing 106516875, recorded 13 hours earlier the same day (2024-12-05 01:33), showed a wide QRS of 144 ms with an rsR' in V1 and wide terminal S waves in I and V6 - right bundle branch block - together with an extreme axis of -177 degrees and QTc 475 ms. The bundle branch block has resolved on the current tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, regular (RR 0.97 s). Low-amplitude but consistent upright P in II, PR 170 ms. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +65 degrees. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad late T wave peaking about 405 ms after QRS onset and ending near 490 ms: QT about 536 ms, Bazett QTc 545 ms. The prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07) had a QTc of 450 ms, so the QTc has risen by about 95 ms, coinciding with amiodarone started 2025-11-10.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 100 bpm. The rhythm is grossly irregularly irregular (RR 0.39-1.07 s, RMSSD 243 ms) and there is no organised atrial activity - the TP segments are flat with no P waves on the averaged beat, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -49 degrees (left axis deviation). QT 330 ms, Bazett QTc 427 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm, regular. Prominent upright P in II (0.22 mV), PR 142 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +39 degrees. QT 340 ms at RR 0.58 s, Bazett QTc 447 ms. Sinus tachycardia at 108 bpm. Upright P wave in II (0.12 mV) before each QRS, PR about 120 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees. QT 336 ms at RR 0.55 s, Bazett QTc 451 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response at about 136 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.35-0.65 s) and there is no discrete P wave in any lead on the averaged beat, so no PR interval is measurable. Regular rhythm at 70 bpm with a consistent atrial complex before each QRS at PR about 144 ms. Regular rhythm at 70 bpm with a consistent atrial complex before each QRS at PR about 144 ms. Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 0.87 s, RR variability under 1 per cent) with a low-amplitude atrial deflection preceding each QRS at a fixed interval of about 160 ms. The P wave is positive in I and aVL but negative in II, III and aVF (P axis roughly -45 degrees), which is not a sinus P axis: this is an ectopic low/left atrial rhythm rather than sinus rhythm. QRS 66 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -24 degrees. QT 410 ms, Bazett QTc 439 ms. The prior tracing 104232242 (2025-04-27) showed a rate of 61 bpm with markedly different limb-lead polarity (deep S in lead I, axis -175 degrees, suggesting arm-lead reversal on that study) and a QTc of 414 ms; no atrial fibrillation, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block on either study, and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm, regular (RR 0.62 s). Upright P wave in II (0.19 mV), PR about 116 ms. QRS 68 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +5 degrees. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.
Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR 0.83 s). Upright P in II, PR 144 ms. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +21 degrees. QT 382 ms, Bazett QTc 419 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response at about 151 bpm. The prior ECG 107374881 (2025-09-12, the previous day) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with an upright P in II and PR about 155 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm. Tall upright P in II (0.21 mV), PR 170 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +11 degrees. QT 374 ms at RR 0.83 s, Bazett QTc 409 ms. Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular (RR 0.81 s). Upright P in II, PR about 190 ms (upper normal). QRS 82 ms with a deep S wave in lead I; no bundle branch block. Axis +57 degrees. QT 394 ms, Bazett QTc 437 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, metronomically regular (RR 0.538 s, RR variability 0.2 per cent). A discrete atrial complex precedes each QRS - upright in II (0.20 mV) and biphasic in V1 - with PR about 166 ms; the T wave is inverted in II and upright in V1, which accounts for the unusual-looking baseline, and there is no sawtooth flutter activity. The prior ECG 102955795 (2022-07-04) is very similar (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 415 ms), so there is no change.

Sinus rhythm at a mean rate of 62 bpm. The baseline cycle length is constant at about 0.97 s with one early beat (RR 0.54 s) followed by a compensatory pause (RR 1.39 s) - a single atrial/ventricular ectopic beat. A broad upright P wave is present in II and I before each conducted beat with a PR interval of about 200 ms (upper limit of normal). QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -30 degrees (just within normal). QT 410 ms, Bazett QTc 416 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison. There is no atrial fibrillation on this tracing despite the paroxysmal AF diagnosis.

Regular rhythm at 70 bpm with a consistent atrial complex before each QRS at PR about 144 ms. The limb leads show a globally inverted pattern - lead I is almost entirely negative (S 1.4 mV), aVR is positive, and the P wave is negative in I and II - while the praecordial leads are unremarkable; this pattern is typical of right/left arm lead reversal (dextrocardia is the alternative). Taken at face value the frontal QRS axis is -173 degrees, i.e. in the extreme (northwest) quadrant. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block. QT 358 ms at RR 0.86 s, Bazett QTc 385 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm. Upright P in II, PR 154 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +39 degrees. Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR 0.88 s). Upright P in II (0.14 mV), PR about 140 ms. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +59 degrees. interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 0.66-0.86 s). Upright P wave in II (0.21 mV) before every QRS, PR 185 ms. Narrow QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal QRS axis +47 degrees (normal). QT 340 ms at RR 0.74 s gives a Bazett QTc of 395 ms. This is the patient's only ECG, so there is no prior tracing for comparison. Concordant with the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm, regular. Prominent upright P in II (0.22 mV), PR 142 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +39 degrees. QT 340 ms at RR 0.58 s, Bazett QTc 447 ms. The prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with a QTc of 592 ms; the QTc has fallen by about 145 ms, a decrease of more than 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 108 bpm. Upright P wave in II (0.12 mV) before each QRS, PR about 120 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees. QT 336 ms at RR 0.55 s, Bazett QTc 451 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response at about 136 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.35-0.65 s) and there is no discrete P wave in any lead on the averaged beat, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +8 degrees. There is widespread rate-related ST depression. QT about 292 ms, Bazett QTc 440 ms. The prior tracing 107914094, recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same day, is also atrial fibrillation at 132 bpm with QTc 443 ms, so there is no change. Note that the clinic note of 2026-06-10 describes this study as normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which the tracings contradict.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 0.87 s, RR variability under 1 per cent) with a low-amplitude atrial deflection preceding each QRS at a fixed interval of about 160 ms. The P wave is positive in I and aVL but negative in II, III and aVF (P axis roughly -45 degrees), which is not a sinus P axis: this is an ectopic low/left atrial rhythm rather than sinus rhythm. QRS 66 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -24 degrees. QT 410 ms, Bazett QTc 439 ms. The prior tracing 104232242 (2025-04-27) showed a rate of 61 bpm with markedly different limb-lead polarity (deep S in lead I, axis -175 degrees, suggesting arm-lead reversal on that study) and a QTc of 414 ms; no atrial fibrillation, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block on either study, and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm, regular (RR 0.62 s). Upright P wave in II (0.19 mV), PR about 116 ms. QRS 68 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +5 degrees. The T wave has a prominent late low-amplitude component; measuring to the end of the T wave gives QT about 370 ms and a Bazett QTc of about 470 ms (measuring by the tangent method to the steep limb alone would give roughly 380 ms). Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.
Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR 0.83 s). Upright P in II, PR 144 ms. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +21 degrees. QT 382 ms, Bazett QTc 419 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a controlled ventricular response, mean rate about 61 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.69-1.16 s, RMSSD 288 ms) and there are no P waves, so no PR interval can be given. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +27 degrees. Repolarisation is prolonged: on the long-cycle beats the T wave ends about 500-510 ms after QRS onset, giving QT roughly 530-545 ms at RR about 1.14 s and a Bazett QTc of about 505 ms. The prior ECG 107873952 (2024-11-12, three days earlier) was sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with PR 178 ms and QTc 418 ms, so this tracing shows new atrial fibrillation and a QTc increase of more than 60 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with sinus arrhythmia. Tall upright P in II (0.21 mV), PR about 112 ms. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +62 degrees. QT 424 ms at RR 1.03 s, Bazett QTc 418 ms. The prior ECG 106045460 (2025-03-08, one day earlier) is essentially identical (sinus 62 bpm, PR 112 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 438 ms); no change.

Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, regular (RR 0.72 s). Upright P in II (0.12 mV), PR 154 ms. Narrow QRS 60 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +53 degrees. QT 338 ms, Bazett QTc 398 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 76 bpm, regular (RR 0.78 s). Prominent upright P in II (0.27 mV), PR 154 ms. QRS 64 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +63 degrees. The T wave is broad with a long terminal limb ending about 440 ms after QRS onset: QT about 466 ms, Bazett QTc about 526 ms (prolonged). The prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02) had a QTc of 538 ms, so the QTc is essentially unchanged (-12 ms) and there is no change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, perfectly regular (RR 0.50 s). Upright P in II (0.21 mV) preceding each QRS with PR about 190 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +49 degrees. QT 282 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. Compared with the prior tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 175 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 424 ms, axis +49) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or repolarisation (QTc change -24 ms).

Sinus bradycardia at 55 bpm (RR 1.10 s). An upright P wave in II (0.10 mV) precedes each QRS but the PR interval is prolonged at about 215 ms, consistent with first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms with a dominant R wave in V1 (0.65 mV); no bundle branch block by duration. Axis +8 degrees. QT 408 ms, Bazett QTc 389 ms. The prior ECG 103042067 (2024-11-30) was sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm with PR about 190 ms, QRS 80 ms and QTc 369 ms - no new bundle branch block and no QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response at about 151 bpm. RR intervals vary from 0.29 to 0.58 s with no pattern and there is no organised atrial activity, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 66 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -5 degrees. QT 248 ms at mean RR 0.40 s, Bazett QTc 394 ms. The prior ECG 107374881 (2025-09-12, the previous day) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with an upright P in II and PR about 155 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm. Tall upright P in II (0.21 mV), PR 170 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +11 degrees. QT 374 ms at RR 0.83 s, Bazett QTc 409 ms. The prior ECG 105362569 (2025-11-21) was sinus rhythm at 67 bpm with a QTc of 539 ms; the QTc has fallen by about 130 ms, a decrease of more than 60 ms. Concordant with the 2025-11-23 note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular (RR 0.81 s). Upright P in II, PR about 190 ms (upper normal). QRS 82 ms with a deep S wave in lead I; no bundle branch block. Axis +57 degrees. QT 394 ms, Bazett QTc 437 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, metronomically regular (RR 0.538 s, RR variability 0.2 per cent). A discrete atrial complex precedes each QRS - upright in II (0.20 mV) and biphasic in V1 - with PR about 166 ms; the T wave is inverted in II and upright in V1, which accounts for the unusual-looking baseline, and there is no sawtooth flutter activity. QRS 86 ms with a very deep S in V1 (2.9 mV); no bundle branch block. Axis +36 degrees. QT 310 ms, Bazett QTc 423 ms. The prior ECG 102955795 (2022-07-04) is very similar (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 415 ms), so there is no change.

Sinus rhythm at a mean rate of 62 bpm. The baseline cycle length is constant at about 0.97 s with one early beat (RR 0.54 s) followed by a compensatory pause (RR 1.39 s) - a single atrial/ventricular ectopic beat. A broad upright P wave is present in II and I before each conducted beat with a PR interval of about 200 ms (upper limit of normal). QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -30 degrees (just within normal). QT 410 ms, Bazett QTc 416 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison. There is no atrial fibrillation on this tracing despite the paroxysmal AF diagnosis.

Regular rhythm at 70 bpm with a consistent atrial complex before each QRS at PR about 144 ms. The limb leads show a globally inverted pattern - lead I is almost entirely negative (S 1.4 mV), aVR is positive, and the P wave is negative in I and II - while the praecordial leads are unremarkable; this pattern is typical of right/left arm lead reversal (dextrocardia is the alternative). Taken at face value the frontal QRS axis is -173 degrees, i.e. in the extreme (northwest) quadrant. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block. QT 358 ms at RR 0.86 s, Bazett QTc 385 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm. Upright P in II, PR 154 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +39 degrees. Repolarisation is prolonged - the T wave peaks about 355 ms after QRS onset and ends near 455 ms, giving QT about 492 ms at RR 0.86 s and a Bazett QTc of about 533 ms. The prior ECG 107149156 (2020-06-17) was sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with a QTc of 410 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. Relevant because the patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR 0.88 s). Upright P in II (0.14 mV), PR about 140 ms. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +59 degrees. There is T-wave inversion in leads I, aVL and V1-V2; QT about 432 ms, Bazett QTc 460 ms (mildly prolonged but below 500 ms). Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison. This is the ECG obtained after escitalopram was started on 2026-02-12.

Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm (RR 1.13 s). Upright P in II (0.19 mV), PR 176 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -6 degrees. QT 394 ms, Bazett QTc 370 ms. The prior ECG 108651109 (2018-12-13) showed sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with PR about 202 ms, QRS 88 ms and QTc 399 ms; no new bundle branch block, no arrhythmia and no QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular. Upright P in II (0.15 mV), PR 130 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +45 degrees. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged: T wave peaks about 370 ms after QRS onset and ends near 465 ms, giving QT about 494 ms at RR 0.88 s and a Bazett QTc of about 526 ms. The previous ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23) had a QTc of 370 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. Clinically relevant because the patient takes escitalopram (QT watch-list drug).

Sinus tachycardia at 141 bpm. The rhythm is regular (RR 0.40-0.45 s, RR variability 2 per cent) and a small upright P wave is visible in lead II about 125-140 ms before each QRS; the preceding negative deflection in II with a positive counterpart in V1 is this patient's inverted T wave, which has the same polarity on his earlier tracings. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +2 degrees. QT 266 ms, Bazett QTc 407 ms. The prior ECG 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation at 105 bpm with grossly irregular RR intervals and no P waves, so the atrial fibrillation has resolved (QTc change -15 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular (RR 0.73 s). Upright P in II (0.14 mV), PR 160 ms. QRS 96 ms - slightly widened but below 120 ms, so no bundle branch block. Axis +30 degrees. QT 386 ms, Bazett QTc 452 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR 0.50 s). A discrete upright P wave in II precedes each QRS with PR about 140 ms; atrial activity is 1:1 with the ventricles and phase locked, excluding flutter. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +68 degrees. There is marked ST depression inferolaterally. QT about 294 ms, Bazett QTc 417 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm. Upright P in II (0.17 mV), PR 148 ms. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +57 degrees. QT 350 ms at RR 0.59 s, Bazett QTc 455 ms. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day (2021-08-23 10:06) and is essentially identical (sinus 100 bpm, PR 148 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 452 ms), so there is no interval change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular (RR 1.16 s). Upright P in II, PR 170 ms. QRS 84 ms with a tall R in V6 (3.3 mV) meeting voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy; no bundle branch block. Axis +35 degrees. QT 440 ms, Bazett QTc 408 ms. Prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) showed sinus bradycardia 58 bpm with an atrial ectopic beat, QRS 82 ms, QTc 422 ms - no significant change.

Sinus tachycardia at 122 bpm, regular. Upright P in II (0.15 mV), PR about 130 ms. QRS is now narrow at 86 ms; frontal axis +137 degrees (right axis deviation) with an rS pattern in lead I. QT 302 ms, Bazett QTc 430 ms. The prior tracing 106516875, recorded 13 hours earlier the same day (2024-12-05 01:33), showed a wide QRS of 144 ms with an rsR' in V1 and wide terminal S waves in I and V6 - right bundle branch block - together with an extreme axis of -177 degrees and QTc 475 ms. The bundle branch block has resolved on the current tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, regular (RR 0.97 s). Low-amplitude but consistent upright P in II, PR 170 ms. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +65 degrees. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad late T wave peaking about 405 ms after QRS onset and ending near 490 ms: QT about 536 ms, Bazett QTc 545 ms. The prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07) had a QTc of 450 ms, so the QTc has risen by about 95 ms, coinciding with amiodarone started 2025-11-10.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 100 bpm. The rhythm is grossly irregularly irregular (RR 0.39-1.07 s, RMSSD 243 ms) and there is no organised atrial activity - the TP segments are flat with no P waves on the averaged beat, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -49 degrees (left axis deviation). QT 330 ms, Bazett QTc 427 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 (DocumentReference 96cdf346) states: ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: ECG 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13:50) and ECG 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36:45) each show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation at about 130-140 bpm (RR intervals ranging 0.35-0.72 s). The documented rhythm and rate are both inconsistent with the same-day tracings.

His most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 536 ms and RR 0.97 s, giving a Bazett QTc of about 545 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo (clinic document 615f2777). QTc was 444 ms on the preceding tracing (108780865, 2025-06-07), i.e. a marked interval increase after amiodarone was started on 2025-11-10. Most recent electrolytes are normal (potassium 4.3 mmol/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, both 2026-06-09), so prescriber review of the amiodarone is required.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 0.66-0.86 s). Upright P wave in II (0.21 mV) before every QRS, PR 185 ms. Narrow QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal QRS axis +47 degrees (normal). QT 340 ms at RR 0.74 s gives a Bazett QTc of 395 ms. This is the patient's only ECG, so there is no prior tracing for comparison. Concordant with the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm, regular. Prominent upright P in II (0.22 mV), PR 142 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +39 degrees. QT 340 ms at RR 0.58 s, Bazett QTc 447 ms. The prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with a QTc of 592 ms; the QTc has fallen by about 145 ms, a decrease of more than 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 108 bpm. Upright P wave in II (0.12 mV) before each QRS, PR about 120 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees. QT 336 ms at RR 0.55 s, Bazett QTc 451 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response at about 136 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.35-0.65 s) and there is no discrete P wave in any lead on the averaged beat, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +8 degrees. There is widespread rate-related ST depression. QT about 292 ms, Bazett QTc 440 ms. The prior tracing 107914094, recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same day, is also atrial fibrillation at 132 bpm with QTc 443 ms, so there is no change. Note that the clinic note of 2026-06-10 describes this study as normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which the tracings contradict.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 0.87 s, RR variability under 1 per cent) with a low-amplitude atrial deflection preceding each QRS at a fixed interval of about 160 ms. The P wave is positive in I and aVL but negative in II, III and aVF (P axis roughly -45 degrees), which is not a sinus P axis: this is an ectopic low/left atrial rhythm rather than sinus rhythm. QRS 66 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -24 degrees. QT 410 ms, Bazett QTc 439 ms. The prior tracing 104232242 (2025-04-27) showed a rate of 61 bpm with markedly different limb-lead polarity (deep S in lead I, axis -175 degrees, suggesting arm-lead reversal on that study) and a QTc of 414 ms; no atrial fibrillation, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block on either study, and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm, regular (RR 0.62 s). Upright P wave in II (0.19 mV), PR about 116 ms. QRS 68 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +5 degrees. The T wave has a prominent late low-amplitude component; measuring to the end of the T wave gives QT about 370 ms and a Bazett QTc of about 470 ms (measuring by the tangent method to the steep limb alone would give roughly 380 ms). Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.
Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR 0.83 s). Upright P in II, PR 144 ms. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +21 degrees. QT 382 ms, Bazett QTc 419 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a controlled ventricular response, mean rate about 61 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.69-1.16 s, RMSSD 288 ms) and there are no P waves, so no PR interval can be given. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +27 degrees. Repolarisation is prolonged: on the long-cycle beats the T wave ends about 500-510 ms after QRS onset, giving QT roughly 530-545 ms at RR about 1.14 s and a Bazett QTc of about 505 ms. The prior ECG 107873952 (2024-11-12, three days earlier) was sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with PR 178 ms and QTc 418 ms, so this tracing shows new atrial fibrillation and a QTc increase of more than 60 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with sinus arrhythmia. Tall upright P in II (0.21 mV), PR about 112 ms. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +62 degrees. QT 424 ms at RR 1.03 s, Bazett QTc 418 ms. The prior ECG 106045460 (2025-03-08, one day earlier) is essentially identical (sinus 62 bpm, PR 112 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 438 ms); no change.

Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, regular (RR 0.72 s). Upright P in II (0.12 mV), PR 154 ms. Narrow QRS 60 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +53 degrees. QT 338 ms, Bazett QTc 398 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 76 bpm, regular (RR 0.78 s). Prominent upright P in II (0.27 mV), PR 154 ms. QRS 64 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +63 degrees. The T wave is broad with a long terminal limb ending about 440 ms after QRS onset: QT about 466 ms, Bazett QTc about 526 ms (prolonged). The prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02) had a QTc of 538 ms, so the QTc is essentially unchanged (-12 ms) and there is no change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, perfectly regular (RR 0.50 s). Upright P in II (0.21 mV) preceding each QRS with PR about 190 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +49 degrees. QT 282 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. Compared with the prior tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 175 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 424 ms, axis +49) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or repolarisation (QTc change -24 ms).

Sinus bradycardia at 55 bpm (RR 1.10 s). An upright P wave in II (0.10 mV) precedes each QRS but the PR interval is prolonged at about 215 ms, consistent with first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms with a dominant R wave in V1 (0.65 mV); no bundle branch block by duration. Axis +8 degrees. QT 408 ms, Bazett QTc 389 ms. The prior ECG 103042067 (2024-11-30) was sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm with PR about 190 ms, QRS 80 ms and QTc 369 ms - no new bundle branch block and no QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response at about 151 bpm. RR intervals vary from 0.29 to 0.58 s with no pattern and there is no organised atrial activity, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 66 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -5 degrees. QT 248 ms at mean RR 0.40 s, Bazett QTc 394 ms. The prior ECG 107374881 (2025-09-12, the previous day) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with an upright P in II and PR about 155 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm. Tall upright P in II (0.21 mV), PR 170 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +11 degrees. QT 374 ms at RR 0.83 s, Bazett QTc 409 ms. The prior ECG 105362569 (2025-11-21) was sinus rhythm at 67 bpm with a QTc of 539 ms; the QTc has fallen by about 130 ms, a decrease of more than 60 ms. Concordant with the 2025-11-23 note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular (RR 0.81 s). Upright P in II, PR about 190 ms (upper normal). QRS 82 ms with a deep S wave in lead I; no bundle branch block. Axis +57 degrees. QT 394 ms, Bazett QTc 437 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, metronomically regular (RR 0.538 s, RR variability 0.2 per cent). A discrete atrial complex precedes each QRS - upright in II (0.20 mV) and biphasic in V1 - with PR about 166 ms; the T wave is inverted in II and upright in V1, which accounts for the unusual-looking baseline, and there is no sawtooth flutter activity. QRS 86 ms with a very deep S in V1 (2.9 mV); no bundle branch block. Axis +36 degrees. QT 310 ms, Bazett QTc 423 ms. The prior ECG 102955795 (2022-07-04) is very similar (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 415 ms), so there is no change.

Sinus rhythm at a mean rate of 62 bpm. The baseline cycle length is constant at about 0.97 s with one early beat (RR 0.54 s) followed by a compensatory pause (RR 1.39 s) - a single atrial/ventricular ectopic beat. A broad upright P wave is present in II and I before each conducted beat with a PR interval of about 200 ms (upper limit of normal). QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -30 degrees (just within normal). QT 410 ms, Bazett QTc 416 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison. There is no atrial fibrillation on this tracing despite the paroxysmal AF diagnosis.

Regular rhythm at 70 bpm with a consistent atrial complex before each QRS at PR about 144 ms. The limb leads show a globally inverted pattern - lead I is almost entirely negative (S 1.4 mV), aVR is positive, and the P wave is negative in I and II - while the praecordial leads are unremarkable; this pattern is typical of right/left arm lead reversal (dextrocardia is the alternative). Taken at face value the frontal QRS axis is -173 degrees, i.e. in the extreme (northwest) quadrant. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block. QT 358 ms at RR 0.86 s, Bazett QTc 385 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm. Upright P in II, PR 154 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +39 degrees. Repolarisation is prolonged - the T wave peaks about 355 ms after QRS onset and ends near 455 ms, giving QT about 492 ms at RR 0.86 s and a Bazett QTc of about 533 ms. The prior ECG 107149156 (2020-06-17) was sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with a QTc of 410 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. Relevant because the patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR 0.88 s). Upright P in II (0.14 mV), PR about 140 ms. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +59 degrees. There is T-wave inversion in leads I, aVL and V1-V2; QT about 432 ms, Bazett QTc 460 ms (mildly prolonged but below 500 ms). Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison. This is the ECG obtained after escitalopram was started on 2026-02-12.

Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm (RR 1.13 s). Upright P in II (0.19 mV), PR 176 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -6 degrees. QT 394 ms, Bazett QTc 370 ms. The prior ECG 108651109 (2018-12-13) showed sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with PR about 202 ms, QRS 88 ms and QTc 399 ms; no new bundle branch block, no arrhythmia and no QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular. Upright P in II (0.15 mV), PR 130 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +45 degrees. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged: T wave peaks about 370 ms after QRS onset and ends near 465 ms, giving QT about 494 ms at RR 0.88 s and a Bazett QTc of about 526 ms. The previous ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23) had a QTc of 370 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. Clinically relevant because the patient takes escitalopram (QT watch-list drug).

Sinus tachycardia at 141 bpm. The rhythm is regular (RR 0.40-0.45 s, RR variability 2 per cent) and a small upright P wave is visible in lead II about 125-140 ms before each QRS; the preceding negative deflection in II with a positive counterpart in V1 is this patient's inverted T wave, which has the same polarity on his earlier tracings. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +2 degrees. QT 266 ms, Bazett QTc 407 ms. The prior ECG 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation at 105 bpm with grossly irregular RR intervals and no P waves, so the atrial fibrillation has resolved (QTc change -15 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular (RR 0.73 s). Upright P in II (0.14 mV), PR 160 ms. QRS 96 ms - slightly widened but below 120 ms, so no bundle branch block. Axis +30 degrees. QT 386 ms, Bazett QTc 452 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular (RR 0.66 s). Upright P in II (0.14 mV), PR about 170 ms. QRS 74 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -17 degrees. QT 352 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms. The prior ECG 102616671 (2021-05-16) was sinus rhythm at 87 bpm with PR 146 ms, QRS 76 ms and QTc 410 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR 0.50 s). A discrete upright P wave in II precedes each QRS with PR about 140 ms; atrial activity is 1:1 with the ventricles and phase locked, excluding flutter. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +68 degrees. There is marked ST depression inferolaterally. QT about 294 ms, Bazett QTc 417 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm. Upright P in II (0.17 mV), PR 148 ms. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +57 degrees. QT 350 ms at RR 0.59 s, Bazett QTc 455 ms. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day (2021-08-23 10:06) and is essentially identical (sinus 100 bpm, PR 148 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 452 ms), so there is no interval change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular (RR 1.16 s). Upright P in II, PR 170 ms. QRS 84 ms with a tall R in V6 (3.3 mV) meeting voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy; no bundle branch block. Axis +35 degrees. QT 440 ms, Bazett QTc 408 ms. Prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) showed sinus bradycardia 58 bpm with an atrial ectopic beat, QRS 82 ms, QTc 422 ms - no significant change.

Sinus tachycardia at 122 bpm, regular. Upright P in II (0.15 mV), PR about 130 ms. QRS is now narrow at 86 ms; frontal axis +137 degrees (right axis deviation) with an rS pattern in lead I. QT 302 ms, Bazett QTc 430 ms. The prior tracing 106516875, recorded 13 hours earlier the same day (2024-12-05 01:33), showed a wide QRS of 144 ms with an rsR' in V1 and wide terminal S waves in I and V6 - right bundle branch block - together with an extreme axis of -177 degrees and QTc 475 ms. The bundle branch block has resolved on the current tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, regular (RR 0.97 s). Low-amplitude but consistent upright P in II, PR 170 ms. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +65 degrees. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad late T wave peaking about 405 ms after QRS onset and ending near 490 ms: QT about 536 ms, Bazett QTc 545 ms. The prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07) had a QTc of 450 ms, so the QTc has risen by about 95 ms, coinciding with amiodarone started 2025-11-10.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 100 bpm. The rhythm is grossly irregularly irregular (RR 0.39-1.07 s, RMSSD 243 ms) and there is no organised atrial activity - the TP segments are flat with no P waves on the averaged beat, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -49 degrees (left axis deviation). QT 330 ms, Bazett QTc 427 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

arguments.explanation: Sinus rhythm/sinus bradycardia at a mean 59 bpm. An upright P wave precedes each QRS with a prolonged PR of about 215 ms (first-degree AV block). The QRS is wide at 124 ms with a broad monophasic R wave in I and V6, absent septal q waves and deep QS complexes in V1-V2 - left bundle branch block. Axis -21 degrees. The prior ECG 103686933 (2024-06-03) shows exactly the same pattern (sinus 68 bpm, PR about 220 ms, LBBB with QRS 126 ms, QTc 517 ms), so there is no new or resolved bundle branch block and the QTc change (-45 ms) is less than 60 ms.
